chapter_theme: The descending states of the soul (கீழால் அவத்தை): waking, dream, deep sleep, turiya and the beyond are placed at centres of the body from the brow downward, each with fewer instruments; bound by the five malas the soul is born and dies without end, yet the Lord rouses it from the stupor of anava through maya, and one who sees the malas plainly in full waking stands with the Supreme.
structure_note: Places and instruments of the states (2142 to 2147); an interlude on ignorance of the life in the body and on yogic mastery of breath and elements (2148 to 2153); the states one by one from dream to the beyond (2154 to 2159); the malas, the kevala state and the Lord's awakening of the soul (2160 to 2166).

2142.reading: Waking, with its twenty-five, is at the middle place; dream, with its fourteen, they say is at the throat; deep sleep is in the heart of the purusha who sees no falsehood; and turiya is at the navel of the one who has seen the truth.
2142.nuance: மத்திமை is traditionally the brow. ஐஐந்து may be twenty-five or five and five, and the usual Siddhanta count for waking is thirty-five; சுழுனை here seems to stand for deep sleep (சுழுத்தி) rather than the channel sushumna.

2143.reading: Counting from the thirty-six, the states run from first waking as five, then four, then two and one; understand them as reaching from niyati up to Siva.
2143.nuance: The numbers (ஐந்து, நான்கு, இரண்டு, ஒன்று) are compressed and their objects are not named; நியதி and சிவம் are the ends of the tattva list, so the verse seems to map the states onto the tattvas. அப்பதி is unclear.

2144.reading: The ten senses, their ten objects, the ten vital airs that stand as mantra, the four inner instruments and the soul make up the bound state of waking.
2144.nuance: The sum is thirty-five, the traditional count of waking's instruments. மந்திரமாய் நின்ற மாருதம் (breath standing as mantra) is usually linked to the unspoken mantra of the breath. பந்த names waking itself as bondage.

2145.reading: Earth is golden, water white, fire red, air black and the sky smoke-coloured, and those who stand in them remain hidden.
2145.nuance: பசுமை (green) in line 1 has no clear element of its own; it may qualify earth or be a slip. The ones who stand hidden (மறைந்துநின்றார்) are traditionally the deities presiding over the elements.

2146.reading: The five elements, the five senses, the outer tattvas that work harm, the malas, the gunas and the adharas: the instruments of the first state number ninety-six.
2146.nuance: Ninety-six is the larger Siddhanta count of the tattvas and their sub-parts (2179 calls it common to all). ஏதம் படஞ்செய்து is obscure; it may say the instruments cause harm or that they spread out.

2147.reading: Told by their places: twenty-five elephants, a great army, five leaping horses, the lord in the middle with four who dwell within, and at the long gate five with four.
2147.nuance: The body is pictured as a king's camp. Tradition takes the elephants as the tattvas, the horses as the senses or breaths, the lord as the soul and the four as the inner instruments; the closing five with four is unclear.

2148.reading: People cling to body after body and do not know the life that stands within the body; not knowing the bond between body and life, they wander bewildered like a dog that has strayed into a monastery.
2148.nuance: உடம்பும் உடம்பும் உடம்பைத் தழுவி may be bodies embracing in desire or the soul taking body after body. The phrase உடம்பொடு உயிரிடை நட்பு is the Kural's (338). The dog in the மடம் is a stray in a place not meant for it.

2149.reading: Fools do not know the one way things stand: if one turns back the ajapa breath, draws it up, holds it as a seed and turns toward Siva the foe of Kama, the body that has taken form will not perish.
2149.nuance: அசபை is the mantra said by the breath without utterance; மாற்றி (reversing) is taken as turning it back inward. மருக்கும் and கருக்கொண்டு are unclear. The promise that the body will not perish is the yogic claim of 724, not a statement about the soul.

2150.reading: The noble teacher who gave the fourteen came within me, and by the kalas he grants he hid away the sixty and set my mind in stillness.
2150.nuance: ஆரியன் is the guru. The fourteen may be the instruments of dream (2154); அறுபத்து (sixty) and ஒடுங்கிய சித்து are not explained in the verse.

2151.reading: Earth, water, fire, air and sky, and the abiding mind, intellect and ego, each contemplated one by one: so mastery of the elements is won.
2151.nuance: பூதசயம் is bhuta-jaya, mastery of the elements, a yogic attainment. The words linked to each element (மலர், பொன்) may name their colours or seats; their exact sense is unclear.

2152.reading: One son to the first, two to the form, three to fire, four to the marriage, five children to the maiden, none before; and the maiden loved the maiden.
2152.nuance: A riddle. The counts one to five are traditionally taken as the qualities of the elements, from sky (sound alone) to earth (all five). The last line, a maiden loving a maiden, is obscure; it may speak of Shakti turning to herself.

2153.reading: Once the five senses, the five objects they mingle with and the four inner instruments are understood together, he becomes as he was of old and abides spread out as the whole cosmos.
2153.nuance: It is unclear whether the subject is the soul regaining its original state or the Lord. வியாக்கிரத்து is obscure, perhaps for வியாபகம் (pervasion).

2154.reading: As ten of the fourteen fall away and the four inner instruments remain, the soul at the throat sees dream, made from the impressions of household life.
2154.nuance: The ten that leave are taken as the outer senses, so dream works with the inner instruments alone. வாதனை (impressions) makes dream the replay of waking life. மன்று கலந்த is unclear.

2155.reading: Leaving its place and entering the heart alone, its self-regard gone, its understanding gone and dazed, in the unmanifest where it knows nothing spread out, the body forgotten, it is deep sleep.
2155.nuance: அவ்வியத்தம் is the unmanifest. கழுத்தியது, read here as deep sleep, looks like a misprint for சுழுத்தியது; it could also be read with கழுத்து (throat), which would not fit the heart of line 1.

2156.reading: In deep sleep three remain, the chitta, the breath and the soul's own seeing; dwelling within the lotus, the soul stands joined with the excellent reality.
2156.nuance: கழுமுனை may be deep sleep, as in 2142, or the channel sushumna. The lotus is traditionally the heart. விழுமப் பொருள் (the excellent thing) may be the Lord, present even in deep sleep.

2157.reading: Rising from its place into the sky of turiya and leaving the world behind, at the summit of thought the soul casts off the ignorance of the flesh and stands silent as a mute.
2157.nuance: ஊமன் (the mute) gives the silence of the state beyond speech. கானத்து எழுந்த (risen in the forest, or in song) is unclear.

2158.reading: When the silent letter meets the spoken letter, the five draw in as a tortoise draws in its limbs; reaching Om it gains an inner light, and it is beyond names, beyond our knowing.
2158.nuance: ஊமை எழுத்து and பேசும் எழுத்து are traditionally the unspoken and spoken parts of a mantra, or bindu and nada. The tortoise is the Kural's image (126) for restraint of the senses; here the drawing-in follows the mantra rather than effort.

2159.reading: Turiya lies within waking itself; the fourteen jackals ate poison and died, the great horse bolted and was gone, and where turiya ends cannot be told.
2159.nuance: The fourteen jackals are taken as the fourteen instruments and the horse as the breath or mind. The first line makes turiya a state reached awake, not a separate sleep.

2160.reading: Held in the states by the five unyielding malas and given body and instruments from maya that are other than itself, every soul is born and dies without end and is beaten by strong deeds that do not abate.
2160.nuance: Tirumular counts five malas (2183 names anava first); tradition lists anava, karma, maya, the concealing power and mayeya. வேறாய stresses that body and instruments are not the soul.

2161.reading: Maya makes the soul eat the fruit of its deeds without itself being part of the soul, and release comes by the Lord's grace: the soul, born through knowledge, reaches release directly through the knowledge it contemplates.
2161.nuance: Line 1 and நண்ணல் இலா உயிர் (the soul that does not approach, or the soul not yet near) are compressed. The verse joins grace and knowledge as the means of release without saying how they relate.

2162.reading: In the kevala state anava is a sleep of utter stupor; as it gives way, the knowing soul, prompted by its karma, leaves that steady kevala and, not yet the Supreme, falls into the five states.
2162.nuance: கேவலம் is the soul's state alone with anava, before embodiment. நந்த can mean to wane or to flourish, so whether anava weakens or prevails here is open; the reading takes it as waning.

2163.reading: As a teacher wakes with a shining rod the pupils sleeping in front of him, so the loving Lord wakes those long sunk in anava through blameless Maya.
2163.nuance: The simile makes maya the Lord's instrument of grace, not a fault: embodiment wakes the soul from the deeper sleep of anava. ஏசாத (blameless) defends maya against the charge the word often carries.

2164.reading: As the undiscerning speak of the moon seen in the clouds and in a pot of Ganga water as though it were many, though the great moon is one and undiminished, so with this body: its king departs on the day it goes.
2164.nuance: The moon reflected in many vessels is an old image for one reality seen in many bodies. The reading of line 4 (அஞ்சணும் மன்னன் அன்றே போம் அளவே) is a guess; whether the one is the soul or the Lord is unclear.

2165.reading: When the king of the land rides his leaping horse into his fair city, the five who serve him and all who live there take to the drum-house and fall asleep.
2165.nuance: Traditionally the king is the soul, the horse the breath, the city the body and the five the senses, so the verse pictures the senses falling still as the soul withdraws inward. துடியில்லம் (house of the drum, or of the pulse) is unclear.

2166.reading: Considering how the five stubborn malas work through the five long states, one who sees all five plainly while fully awake stands always with the Supreme.
2166.nuance: நேர் (straight, direct, facing) opens every line: the stubborn (நேரா) malas, seen directly (நேரே) in waking, give way to the true (நேராம்) Supreme. The verse places release in waking, not in withdrawal from it.

links.note: Both picture the body as a king's realm with horses and a company of five: in 2147 as the arrayed camp of the waking instruments, in 2165 as a city whose five servants sleep when the king rides in.
2142 places dream at the throat with fourteen instruments; 2154 says which ten fall away and that dream is built from the impressions of household life.
2162 describes anava as a stupor from which the soul falls into the states; 2163 gives the Lord's side: the states are his waking of the sleeper through maya.
2160 says the five malas keep every soul in endless birth and death; 2166 says the same five, seen plainly in waking, are the way to stand with the Supreme.
Tirumular takes the Kural's own phrase, உடம்பொடு உயிரிடை நட்பு. The Kural says that bond ends as a bird leaves its shell; Tirumular faults people who never come to know it.
Both separate the life from the body it lives in: the Naladiyar's dancer leaves the skin bag, and Tirumular's fools cling to bodies without knowing the life inside.
Both use the tortoise drawing in for the five senses held in. In the Kural it is self-restraint that guards through seven births; in Tirumular it follows when the silent and spoken letters meet.
Both treat birth as a waking from sleep. The Kural uses it to show how quickly birth and death alternate; Tirumular makes embodiment the Lord's waking of the soul from anava's deeper sleep.

source_issues: 2158: line 1 begins with a stray Latin 'Y' (Yஊமை); the tool flags it as corrupt.
2155: கழுத்தியது looks like a misprint for சுழுத்தியது (deep sleep).
2145: பசுமை in line 1 is not matched to any element and may be a slip.
2164: line 4 (அஞ்சணும் மன்னன்) is obscure and may be corrupt.
